claim: The use of excessive force by officers negates probable cause for a lawful arrest under § 148(a)(1) only when the excessive force precedes any refusal to comply with ejection, and where such temporal ambiguity exists, individual officers cannot invoke qualified immunity unless it is clearly established that the violation of § 148(a)(1) was completed prior to the application of force.
initial_reasoning: The court’s analysis (Paragraph 4) holds that excessive force used after an arrest for § 148(a)(1) does not negate probable cause and that officers retain qualified immunity even when probable cause is close. This directly contradicts the claim that such force negates probable cause only when it precedes refusal to comply and that qualified immunity fails unless the violation is proven prior to force.
